newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rhone falls on Rorer product recall.
newsitem.headline: Rhone falls on Rorer product recall.

text.p: Shares in chemical group Rhone-Poulenc fell more than three percent after its drugs unit Rhone-Poulenc Rorer recalled a product and issued a profit waring.
Rorer was suspended in New York while it said that its Centeon LCC venture with Hoechst was recalling all lots of its albumin products as a precaution against a risk of bacterial infection.
Rorer said the recall costs and potential lost sales could cut the consensus estimate for its 1996 earnings by 10 to 12 percent. The profit warning hit Rhone shares in Paris as well.
The consenus earnings estimate for Rhone-Poulenc Rorer, as compiled by First Call, was for $3.25 per share against a reported 1995 figure of $2.43
At Rhone-Poulenc in Paris there was no immediate comment on the possible effect on its own earnings.
At 1445 GMT, Rhone-Poulenc was down 4.20 francs at 140.20.
Analysts said that Rhone-Poulenc Rorer made over 55 percent of Rhone-Poulenc's results.
